review.intent_summary: Detect changes in numeric distributions and category composition using explicit populations and bounded causal monitoring while preserving source support and separating statistical evidence from business impact.

criteria.criterion: Numeric comparisons use a tie-aware two-sample empirical distribution test and report effect size, population support and source identities.
Categorical comparisons assess the whole composition and explain changed shares without treating consumed quantities as independent observations.
Causal monitoring freezes an earlier reference, compares bounded recent windows and accounts for all planned looks and window sizes in its testing budget.
Unknown observations and untrusted tied timestamps cannot silently establish sequence continuity, and insufficient or unfinished evidence cannot establish normality.
Results separate statistical evidence, practical effect thresholds and business impact, with inspectable assumptions and reproducible calculations.

verification_evidence: All 31 distribution tests passed across the initial run and isolated retry; the initial temporary-directory permissions error was resolved using a fresh --basetemp.

Manually checked README chapters 25–26, renderer code, fixtures and both PNGs against engine output: unchanged means, population support, first detection at index 182, category shares and weighted-report limits agree.
remaining_gaps: Production detection delay, false-finding burden and validity under clustered or dependent traffic require representative caller-owned replay.
Population comparability, exchangeability and testing-budget continuity across monitors, resets and deployments remain caller responsibilities.
